paper_id: Hierarchical Federated Learning through LAN-WAN Orchestration
title: Hierarchical Federated Learning through LAN-WAN Orchestration
motivation: WAN-driven FL has communication bottleneck and high monetary cost (80% billing to network traffic)
problem_framing: Hierarchical FL with intra-LAN P2P aggregation and infrequent inter-LAN global aggregation across WAN
key_insight: LAN bandwidth is 10x more abundant and unmetered; frequent local aggregation reduces WAN reliance while accelerating convergence
method_signature: LanFL: LAN-aware hierarchical FL with dynamic topology selection and device number balancing for heterogeneous LANs
evaluation_criteria: Model accuracy preservation, convergence speedup (1.5x-6.0x), WAN traffic reduction (18.3x-75.6x), monetary cost reduction (3.8x-27.2x)
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: LanFL only works with LAN domains having at least 10 devices; current design relies on manual parameter tuning; simulation-based without real deployment
evidence_for_taste: Such a cost can be amplified
even worse in FL due to the Non-IID data
thinking_moves: 把WAN瓶颈问题重新frame成利用LAN资源的机会
先分析现有方法的根本缺陷(网络是瓶颈且成本高),再寻找替代资源
用hierarchical结构调和异构网络资源的矛盾
通过实验验证关键设计点的有效性(dynamic device selection等)
